note: Every place two sources part on the board, with what each says, which way this package went and why, and the measurement that would close it.
authority: hardware.json's authority order decides. A divergence records the cases where following it is a choice rather than a reading.

divergences.topic: Which way FFFC's bank shift moves a bank number.

documentSays.claim: Each step of the shift adds eight banks: bank 1 with a shift of 01 reaches bank 9.
documentSays.source: Software Reference Manual for the SEGA Mark III Console, pages 39 and 40

referenceSays.claim: Each step of the shift takes eight banks away, by adding (4 - shift) times eight.
referenceSays.source: Genesis Plus GX core/cart_hw/sms_cart.c, mapper_16k_w, at a5834b3d

thisPackageDid.claim: Adds eight banks per step, as the manual's figure and its note say.
thisPackageDid.why: The manual's note is unambiguous: bank shift 00 with bank 09 is the address bank shift 01 with bank 1 reaches. MAME implements no shift at all, so no second implementation backs Genesis Plus GX's direction, and the census counts whether any image in the library sets the shift.

divergences.wouldCloseIt: On a 4 Mbit Sega cartridge write 01h to FFFC and 01h to FFFF, and compare 8000h with banks 9 and 25.

divergences.topic: Whether FFFC's bits 0 and 1 do anything.

documentSays.claim: They shift every bank number by eight per step.
documentSays.source: Software Reference Manual for the SEGA Mark III Console, page 39

referenceSays.claim: Nothing: only bits 3 and 2 of FFFC are decoded.

thisPackageDid.why: The manual is the first rung and prints the shift with a worked figure.

divergences.topic: How many bits of a frame register select a bank.

documentSays.claim: Five, under three zero bits; page 21 shows three under five.
documentSays.source: Software Reference Manual for the SEGA Mark III Console, pages 21 and 39

referenceSays.claim: All eight, modulo the cartridge's page count.
referenceSays.source: MAME src/devices/bus/sega8/rom.cpp at 94fc55c9692b180dcb608e2e222e48315db5017a; Genesis Plus GX agrees

thisPackageDid.claim: Takes the whole byte modulo the page count.
thisPackageDid.why: The manual's zero bits describe what software should write, not what the mapper ignores, and the library holds images over 512K that page with the upper bits.

divergences.wouldCloseIt: Write 20h to FFFF on a 512K Sega cartridge and compare 8000h with bank 0.

divergences.topic: Which player's second button port DD bit 3 carries.

documentSays.claim: Player 1's, in the joystick table; player 2's, in the trackball table two pages later.
documentSays.source: Software Reference Manual for the SEGA Mark III Console, pages 24 and 26

referenceSays.quote: D3 : Port B TR pin input
referenceSays.source: Genesis Plus GX core/io_ctrl.c, io_z80_read, at a5834b3d

thisPackageDid.why: Player 1's second button already has port DC bit 5 in the same table, the manual's own trackball table gives bit 3 to player 2, and the manual is a retyped copy with other typing errors.

divergences.topic: Whether port 3E bit 4 switches the system RAM off.

documentSays.claim: It does: 0 enables the internal 8K RAM, 1 disables it.
documentSays.quote: Output port $3E controls the memory enables.
documentSays.source: Software Reference Manual for the SEGA Mark III Console, page 19

referenceSays.claim: It does nothing; the RAM always answers.
referenceSays.source: Genesis Plus GX core/io_ctrl.c io_z80_write and core/cart_hw/sms_cart.c sms_cart_switch, at a5834b3d

thisPackageDid.claim: Switches the RAM off, reading FFh and dropping writes.
thisPackageDid.why: The manual is the first rung and names the bit.

divergences.wouldCloseIt: Write 10h more than the current value to port 3E from code in ROM and read C000h.

documentSays.claim: A RAM write protect switch, with a question mark.
documentSays.source: Software Reference Manual for the SEGA Mark III Console, page 39

referenceSays.claim: It maps the cartridge RAM over C000h to FFFFh.
referenceSays.source: Genesis Plus GX core/cart_hw/sms_cart.c, mapper_16k_w, at a5834b3d

thisPackageDid.why: The manual itself is unsure what the bit does, MAME ignores it, and the census counts whether any image sets it.

divergences.wouldCloseIt: Set FFFC bit 4 on a Sega cartridge with RAM and read C000h against both RAMs.
